न: na [491], encl. pron. root of 1st person, see ahám. [w. nas, ‘us,’ cf. νώ, ‘we two,’ Lat. nōs, ‘us.’]

ná, adv. 	—1. not [1122b], 32; 	—1a. in connected sentences or clauses: repeated simply: 978, octies; 6214, 15, quinquies; 6313, 14, 714, ter; 413, 1718, 741, 8017, bis; with ca: na…, na…ca, na ca…, 6216; na…, na ca…, na…, 631; with api: see api 2; with u, 2114; 	—1b. not repeated, but replaced by api ca or vā_api (see these), 212, 634; 	—1c. combinations: na ca, 816; na…ca, 137, 6216; naiva, 2219, 2319, 9610; na vai, 9215; na vā, 9612; na tu, 6413; na tv eva tu, see tu; na ha, 9517; na_iva, not exactly, 935; 	—1d. tantamount to a-in negative cpds [1122b4], as nacira, nātidūra, nādhīta, etc.; 	—1e. at beg. of adversative clause: with adversative conj., 3410; without, 2220, 4113, 9216; 	—1f. in emphatic litotes, 219; 	—1g. substantive verb to be supplied, 325 (asti); --1h. na precedes ced, if it belongs to the protasis, 639; if it immediately follows ced, it must be joined to the apodosis, 189; 	—1i. for prohibitive negative, see mā́; --1j. ná, ‘not,’ coalesces metrically in Veda w. following initial vowel, e. g. 7012, 714, 839; 	—2. like [see 1122d and d2], in this sense Vedic only, 7015, 18, 717, 9, etc.; ná, ‘like,’ does not coalesce metrically in Veda w. following initial vowel. [cf. νη-, Lat. nĕ-, negative prefix in νη-κερδές, ‘gain-less,’ nĕ-fas, ‘not right, wrong’; AS. and Old Eng. ne, ‘not’; AS. nā (ne + ā), ‘not ever, never, no,’ Eng. no; Eng. na- in nathless, AS. nā ϸē lœs, ‘not the less’; Eng. n- in n-ever, n-aught, etc.]
नकिस्: nákis, indecl. subst. pron. 	—1. no one, 781, 7320 ?; 	—2. nothing, 7320 ?; 	—3. even as adv. [see 1117], never, 7511. [ná + kís, see 5042 end.]
नकुल: nakulá, m. Viverra ichneumon, an animal like the polecat, often domesticated, and a bitter foe of serpents and mice.
नक्त: nákta, n. night; -am [1111b], by night. [cf. νύξ, stem νυκτ, Lat. nox, stem nocti, Eng. night.]
नक्ष्: √nakṣ (nákṣati, -te; nanákṣa, nanakṣé). attain unto; w. dyām, mount up to heaven. [collateral form of √2naś, ‘attain.’]
नक्षत्र: nákṣatra, n. 	—1. sīdus, heavenly body, in Veda, of sun as well as of stars; star, 133, 7112; sing. collectively, 7811; constellation; 	—2. asterism of the lunar zodiac, 5910. [perhaps the stars are they that ‘mount up’ to heaven, cf. √nakṣ w. dyām.]
नख: nakhá, m. n. nail (on fingers or toes); claw; talon. [cf. ὄνυξ, stem ὀ-νυχ, Lat. unguis, ‘nail, claw’; AS. nœgel, Eng. nail.]
नखिन्: nakhín, a. having claws; as m. beast with claws. [nakha.]
नगर: nágara, n., and -rī, f. town, city.
नगरोपान्त: nagaropānta, n. neighborhood of the town. [upānta.]
नचिर: na-cira, a. not long; -āt, adv. [1114c], soon. [1122b4.]
नट: naṭa, m. dancer, mime, actor (these form a very despised caste). [√nṛt.]
नड: naḍá or naḻá, m. reed. [Whitney 54: cf. 2nadá and nala.]
नद्: √nad (nádati; nanā́da, nedé; naditá; -nádya). sound; roar; bellow. [see 1nadá and nadī́.]
नद: 1nadá, m. the bellower, i. e. bull. [√nad.]
नदी: nadī́, f. roaring stream; river. [√nad: cf. Νέδα, Νέδων, names of streams.]
नन्द्: √nand (nándati, -te; nanánda; nandiṣyáte; nanditá; -nándya). be glad. + abhi, be glad in; greet joyfully.
नन्दन: nandana, a. gladdening; causing joy; as m. son, 2117; as n. Nandana, or Elysium, the pleasure ground of the gods, esp. of Indra, 4918. [caus. of √nand.]
नन्दि: nandi, m. The Gladsome One, euphemistic epithet of the dreadful god, ŚivaRudra.  [√nand: cf. śiva.]
नन्दिदेव: nandi-deva, m. Nandideva, name of a Brahman. [‘having Śiva as his god.’]
नपात्: nápāt, náptṛ [370], m. 	—1. in Veda, descendant in general; son; grandson, 8718; 	—2. in Skt., grandson, 639. [declension: in Veda, nápāt, nápātam, náptrā, náptṛbhis, etc.; in Skt., náptā, náptāram, náptrā, náptṛbhis, etc.: see 1182d: cf. νέποδες, ‘young ones’; Lat. nepōtem, ‘grandson’; AS. nefa, ‘son's son or brother's son’--supplanted by Old French neveu (Eng. nephew), which in Old Eng. meant ‘son's son’ as well as ‘brother's son.’]
नप्ती: naptī́ [356], f. daughter, 726; granddaughter.  [f. to nápāt: acct, 355b.]
नभस्: nábhas, n. 	—1. mist, clouds; 	—2. atmosphere,  sky. [cf. νέφος, νεφέλη, ‘cloud, mist’; Lat. nūbes, ‘cloud,’ nebula, ‘mist’; AS. nifol, ‘misty, gloomy’; Ger. Nebel, ‘mist’: for mg 2, cf. Ger. Wolken and AS. wolcnu, ‘clouds,’ w. Eng. welkin, ‘sky.’]
नभस्तल: nabhas-tala, n. sky-surface, i. e. sky, see tala.
नम्: √nam (námati, -te; nanā́ma, nemé [794e]; ánaṃsīt; naṃsyáti; natá [954d]; námitum, nántum; natvā́; -námya; namáyati ). bow (intrans.), bend one's self; aim at a person (gen.) with (instr.), 7315; nata, bowed down, bending over, 6819N.; --caus. cause to bow, subdue; namyate, is subdued,  316. + ava, bow down, 3417. + ā, bow down to. + ud, raise one's self up, arise. + sam-ud, rise. + nis, bend out; contort one's self. + pra, make obeisance before (acc.).
नमस्: námas, n. bow, obeisance; adoration (by gesture or word); reverence; used also like the Lat. gloria in the Gloria patri. [√nam.]
नमस्कार: namas-kārá, m. a making of namas; adoration. [1713.]
नमुचि: námuci, m. Namuchi, name of a demon, foe of Indra, 8116, 976.
नयन: nayana, n. eye. [‘leader, organ of sense that leads,’ √nī, 1150. 1a: for mg, cf. ānana, gātra, caraṇa, netra.]
नर: nára, m. man, 321, etc.; at 575, the primal man or spirit. [transition-stem fr. nṛ, 1209a.]
नरपति: nara-pati, m. lord of men; king.
नरवाहन: nara-vāhana, a. subst. having men as his team, drawn by men; epithet and name of Kuvera, god of wealth; name of a king, successor of Śālivāhana.
नरवाहनदत्त: naravāhana-datta, m. Naravāhanadatta,  name of a son of king Udayana.
नरवाहनदत्तचरितमय: naravāhanadattacaritamaya, f. -ī, a. containing the adventures of N. [1225: see maya.]
नरव्याघ्र: nara-vyāghra, m. man-tiger, i. e. brave and noble man. [cf. naraśārdūla: 1280b.]
नरशार्दूल: nara-śārdūla, m. man-tiger, i. e. best among men. [cf. naravyāghra: 1280b.]
नरश्रेष्ठ: nara-śreṣṭha, a. subst. best of men.
नरसूनु: nara-sūnu, f. daughter of the primal man or spirit.
नराधिप: narādhipa, m. lord of men, i. e. king, prince. [adhipa.]
नरेश्वर: nareśvara, m. lord of men, i. e. king, prince. [īśvara.]
नरोत्तम: narottama, a. subst. best of men. [uttama. ]
नर्मद: narmada, a. granting or causing fun; making gladness; f. -dā, Narmadā (called also Revā), the modern Nerbudda river. [narman + da.]
नल: nala, m. reed; Nala, name of a prince of Nishadha. [cf. naḍá, Vedic naḻá.]
नव: 1náva, a. new; of an earthen dish, (fresh, i. e.) unburned. [prob. fr. nú, ‘now,’ q. v.: cf. νέος, Lat. novus, Ger. neu, Eng. new.]
2náva [4834], num. nine. [cf. ἐννέα, Lat. novem, Ger. neun, Eng. nine.]
नवनीत: náva-nīta, n. fresh butter. [perhaps ‘fresh-brought,’ as we say ‘bring the butter,  i. e. make it come,’ in churning.]
नवेदस्: návedas, a. perhaps well-knowing, cognizant of (gen.). [apparently fr. an affirmative particle na-, and vedas: see 12963 end.]
नश्: √1naś (náśyati; nanā́śa, neśús; ánaśat; naṅkṣyáti [936]; naṣṭá; nāśáyati). be missing; get lost; vanish; perish, be ruined. [cf. νεκ-ρός, ‘dead’; Lat. nex, ‘death’; nocēre, ‘harm.’] + vi, get lost; perish; caus. cause to disappear;  bring to nought, 8120.

√2naś (náśati, -te; nanā́śa; ā́naṭ [833]). attain; reach, come up to, 741; w. acchā, draw hither, 7611. [see √1aś, ‘reach’: cf. Lat. nac-tus sum, ‘am having reached’; AS. neāh, comp. neār, superl. neāhst, Eng. nigh, near (as comp., Macbeth ii. 3. 146), next; AS. ge-neah, ‘it reaches, es reicht, it suffices’; ge-nōh, Eng. e-nough.] + pra, reach to, hit; fall upon, 788.
नस्: nás [397], f. nose. [nom. dual, nā́sā: cf. Lat. nas-turcium, ‘nose-teaser, nasturtium’; nār-es, ‘nostrils’; AS. nosu, Eng. nose; nos-tril, ‘nose-thrill, nose-hole.’]
nas [491], encl. pron. form of 1st pers. [cf. νώ, ‘we two’; Lat. nōs, ‘us.’] nasa, for nás in cpds [1315c].
नह्: √nah (náhyati [761c]; naddhá [2238]; -náhya). bind; join. [despite naddha (a poss. false formation), and Avestan nazda (Morphologische Untersuchungen, iii. 144), probably for *nagh: cf. Lat. nec-t-ere, ‘bind.’] + upa, tie on, lace.
नहि: nahí, adv. not, to be sure; nahí me ásti, to be sure, I have no…. [ná + hí, 1122a and b4: acct of verb, 595d.]
नहुष: náhuṣa, m. Nahusha, name of an ancient king. [perhaps ‘neighbor,’ from náhus, and in that case a transfer-form (1209b).]
नाक: nā́ka, m. vault of heaven, firmament.
नातिदूर: nātidūra, a. not very far. [na + atidūra, 1122b4.]
नाथ्: √nāth (nā́thate; nāthitá; nā́thitum; -nā́thya). turn with supplication to.
नाथ: nāthá, n. a refuge; as m. protector; lord. [√nāth.]
नाभि: nā́bhi, f. 	—1. navel; 	—2. nave or hub. [cf. ὀμφ-αλός, Lat. umb-ilīcus, AS. naf-ela, Eng. navel; also AS. naf-u, Eng. nave.]
नाभिवर्धन: nābhi-vardhana, n. the cutting of the navel(-string).
नामधेय: nāma-dhéya, n. the name-giving, naming,  599; name, 179, 6022. [nāman.]
नामन्: nā́man, n. 	—1. distinguishing characteristic;  form; 	—2. name, 138, 6021b, 789, 619; nāma grah, (take i. e.) mention the name, 6413; personal name (e. g. devadatta ), as distinguished from the gotra or ‘family name’ (e. g. kāśyapa, ‘descendant of Kaśyapa’), 10319N.; at end of cpds, having…as name, named…, so 11 times, e. g. 1911; 	—3. nāma, adv. [1111b], by name, so 19 times, e. g. 13, 6021a, 9416; also nāmnā, 565; w. interrogatives, pray, 5416. [origin unknown: cf. ὄ-νομα, Lat. nōmen, Eng. name.]
नार: nārá, 	—1. a. human; 	—2. as m. man; --nā́rī, f. woman, 19, 8618, etc.; wife. [nṛ, 1208b: for mg 2, cf. mānava.]
नारद: nārada, m. Nārada, name of an ancient devarṣi (see note to 114), who often appears on the earth to bring news from the gods, and returns to heaven with reports from men.
नारायण: nārāyaṇá, m. Nārāyana, son of the primal man. [simply a patronymic of nara, see 1219.]
नावा: nāvā́, f. ship. [transfer-form (1209, 399) fr. nau, nāv.]
नासा: nā́sā, dual f. the two nostrils, the nose. [transfer-form (399) fr. nás, strong nā́s.]
नासिका: nā́sikā, f. nostril; dual, the two nostrils; the nose. [nā́sā, 1222c 1.]
नास्तिक: nāstika, a. subst. atheist, infidel, not believing the Vedas and Purānas. [fr. na + asti, ‘there is not,’ 1314b.]
नाहुष: nāhuṣa, m. descendant of Nahusha, patronymic of Yayāti. [náhuṣa, 1208 and f.]
नि: ní, prep. down; in, into. [cf. ἐνί, ‘in’; Eng. ne-ther, be-nea-th.]
निकट: nikaṭa, a. near; as n. neighborhood; presence. [1245g.]
निखिल: nikhila, a. entire; all. [perhaps for niḥ-khila, ‘without a gap,’ nis + khila: 13052 end.]
निज: nijá, a. own; belonging to our party, 246; nijo ripus, foe in one's own camp, 3715; often used as reflexive possessive pron., my own, his own, our own, etc., --or rather, my (4717), his (5014, 5312, 564, 6), etc. [perhaps ‘in-born,’ fr. ni + ja.]
निण्य: niṇyá, a. inner; hidden, 7020; as n. secret, 783. [ni.]
नित्य: nítya, a. 	—1. own (Vedic), 7916; 	—2. constant;  eternal, 577; -am, adv. constantly, always, 1716, 6419. [in mg 1, fr. ni, ‘in,’ 1245b, and so signifying ‘inward, not alien.’]
नित्यकाल: nitya-kāla, m. uninterrupted time; -am, adv. always, under all circumstances, 606.
नित्यस्नायिन्: nitya-snāyin, a. constantly making sacred ablutions. [1279.]
निद्: √nid or nind (níndati; ninínda; ánindīt; ninditá; -níndya). blame; reproach. [cf. ὄνειδος, ‘reproach.’]
निधन: nidhána, m. n. end; death, 519. [perhaps fr. √dhā + ni, ‘put down or out of the way,’ ‘make an end of.’]
निबन्धन: nibandhana, n. a binding, ligation, 593; that on which a thing is fastened or rests or depends, condition, means, 467. [√bandh + ni.]
निभृत: nibhṛta, a. (borne down, lowered, i. e.) hidden; -am, adv. secretly. [√bhṛ + ni.]
निमित्त: nimitta, n. mark (for shooting at); sign, token; occasion or cause; -am, -ena, adverbially, because of; tannimittam, -ena, because of this, on account of this.
निमेष: nimeṣá, m. closing or winking of the eyes. [√miṣ + ni.]
नियोग: niyoga, m. a fastening on; injunction, and so, commission; business, 306. [√yuj + ni: for mg, cf. alicui injungere laborem, ‘fasten or impose a task on a person.’]
निर्: nir, for nis before sonants [174]; see nis.
निरन्तर: nir-antara, a. without interval or free space; completely filled, 5310; continuous; uninterrupted, 5612.
निरपाय: nir-apāya, a. without failure or danger; infallible or safe.
निरपेक्ष: nir-apekṣa, a. without regard or expectation;  regardless, 5220; not expecting anything from another, independent, 3117. [apekṣā, 3342.]
निराहार: nir-āhāra, a. without food, abstaining from food.
निरुक्त: nír-ukta, a. spoken out; loud; clear; as n. explanation; etymological interpretation of a word; esp. Nirukta, title of a commentary to the nighaṇṭavas or Vedic Glossary. [√vac + nis.]
निर्गुण: nir-guṇa, a. without a string, 185; void of good qualities, 185; worthless, bad.
निर्भर: nir-bhara, a. 	—1. without measure, much; -am, adv. very; -am prasupta, fast asleep; 	—2. full of.
निर्मल: nir-mala, a. without impurity; pure; clear.
निर्लक्ष्य: nir-lakṣya, a. not to be perceived, avoiding notice. [see nis 3.]
निर्वंश: nir-vaṃśa, a. without family; alone in the world.
निर्विशेष: nir-viśeṣa, a. without distinction; undistinguished;  alike; like.
निर्विशेषाकृति: nirviśeṣākṛti, a. having like appearance,  looking just alike. [ākṛti.]
निवार: nivāra, m. the warding off. [√1vṛ, ‘cover,’ + ni.]
निवीत: nívīta, ppl. hung, i. e. draped, with hangings,  esp. with the sacred cord; as n. [1176a], the wearing the sacred cord about the neck; the sacred cord itself. [√vyā + ni.]
निवृत्त: nivṛtta, ppl. 	—1. turned away; esp. of an action which is turned away, i. e. not directed (to any ulterior purpose or object),  free from hope of reward in this world or the next, disinterested, opp. of pravṛtta, q. v.; 	—2. having turned away from, and so abstaining from, 293. [√vṛt + ni.]
निवेशन: nivéśana, n. a going in and settling down to rest; resting-place; sleeping-place, bed, 1058; dwelling, 86. [√viś + ni: for mg, cf. bhavana.]
निश्चय: niścaya, m. (ascertainment, determination,  i. e.) a fixed opinion or a firm resolve. [poss. fr. √3 ci, ‘notice, look,’ + nis; but better, perhaps, fr. √1ci + nis, and so, ‘an un-piling, i. e. discrimination, determination. ’]
निश्चल: niścala, a. not moving. [nis + cala: see nis 3.]
निश्चित: niścita, ppl. determined, decided; -am, adv. decidedly, surely. [see under niścaya. ]
निःश्रेयस: niḥśreyasa, a. without a superior, i. e. best; as n. final beatitude. [nis + śreyasa: acct, 13053.]
निःश्वास: niḥśvāsa, m. breathing out, expiration; sigh. [√śvas + nis.]
निःश्वासपरम: niḥśvāsa-parama, a. having sighs as chief thing, much addicted to sighing. [1302b.]
निषध: niṣadha, m. pl. the Nishadhans, name of a people; Nishadha, name of a country, 17 N., 43.
निषधाधिप: niṣadhādhipa, m. ruler or king of the Nishadhans. [adhipa.]
निषूदन: niṣūdana, m. finisher (in its colloquial sense), one who makes an end of, destroyer.  [√sūd + ni.]
निषेक: niṣeka, m. an injecting, esp. of semen, impregnation; the ceremony performed upon impregnation. [√sic + ni.]
निषेविन्: niṣevin, a. devoting one's self to; cohabiting with, 6722. [√sev + ni.]
निष्क्रमण: niṣkramaṇa, n. the stepping out; esp. the first going out with a child. [√kram + nis.]
निस्: nís, adv. prep. 	—1. out, forth; 	—2. in cpds [13052 end], having…away, without…,  e. g. nirantara; --3. in cpds, not, e. g. niścala.
नी: √nī (náyati, -te; ninā́ya [800b], ninyé; ánaiṣīt, áneṣṭa [882]; neṣyáti, -te; nītá; nétum; nītvā́; -nī́ya; nīyáte; nāyáyati [1042b]). lead, 2415; guide; conduct, 8520; carry, 3919, etc.; carry off, 3615, 4317; vyāghratāṃ nī, bring to tiger-ness, change into a tiger; vaśaṃ nī, bring into one's power. + anu, (draw along toward one, i. e.) try to win or conciliate by friendly words. + abhi, bring hither to. + ā, bring to, 2914; bring, 319; bring (one liquid) into (another, loc.), mix, 10114; caus. cause to be fetched, 505. + ud, bring up; rescue (as a drowning man from the water), 9010. + upa, take unto one's self, of the teacher who receives a youth of one of the three free castes as pupil, and at the same time invests him with the sacramental cord, thus conferring spiritual rebirth,  and making him a full member of his caste; see upanāyana; upanīta, invested with the sacramental cord. + pari, lead around (a cow, steer), 9114, 10522; esp. lead a bride around the fire (as wedding ceremony), page 99. + pra, 	—1. bring forward; 	—2. as liturgical terminus technicus, convey the sacrificial fire and water to their places on and near the altar; praṇītās (sc. āpas), holy water; 	—3. bring forward (one's feelings), i. e. come out with or manifest one's affection,  915. + vi, lead; guide; train; discipline.
नीच: nīcá, a. low, not high; morally and socially low. [inorganic transfer-form (1209a) fr. nīc-ā́, q. v.]
नीचा: nīcā́, adv. down, low. [adverbially accented instr.--instead of nī́c-ā, 1112e--fr. ny-àñc.]
नीचावयस्: nīcā́-vayas [418], a. whose strength is low; exhausted. [1306.]
नीड: nīḍá, Vedic nīḻá, m. n. 	—1. (place for settling down, i. e.) resting-place; 	—2. esp. bird's nest. [for ni-zd-a, i. e. ni-s(a)d-a --198b3 --√sad + ni: cf. Lat. nīdus, Ger. Nest, Eng. nest: for ḻ, see Whitney 54.]
नीति: nīti, f. 	—1. cónduct, esp. right and sagacious conduct; the knowledge of all that governs virtuous and discreet and statesman-like behavior; political and social ethics; 	—2. leading. [√nī, ‘condúct.’]
नीतिज्ञ: nīti-jñá, a. knowing how to conduct one's self discreetly.
नीतिविद्या: nīti-vidyā, f. knowledge of nīti or political and social ethics, esp. as it concerns princes.
नीतिशास्त्र: nīti-śāstra, n. doctrine or science of political and social ethics.
नीथ: nītha, m. a leading; nīthá, n. (way, and so, like the German Weise) a musical air, song. [√nī, 1163a.]
नीरस: nīrasa, a. sapless, dried up; tasteless; insipid, 5411. [nis + rasa, 174, 179.]
नीरुज्: nīruj, a. without disease; healthy, 223. [nis + rúj, 174, 179.]
नील: nī́la, a. dark-colored, esp. dark blue; as n. indigo; nīlī, f. indigo. [hence, through the Arabic an-nîl, for al-nîl, ‘the indigo-plant, ’ come Eng. anil and aniline.]
नीलसंधानभाण्ड: nīlasaṃdhāna-bhāṇḍa, n. vat for the mixing, i. e. preparing of indigo.
नीवार: nīvā́ra, m. wild rice; sing. the plant; pl. the grains.
नु: √nu (návate; nunā́va; ánūṣṭa; nutá; -nútya). cry aloud; shout; exult; praise. + pra, murmur; hum; esp. utteṛ the sacred syllable om.

nú, adv. 	—1a. now, at once, temporal; 	—1b. now, continuative; adhā nu, so now, 798; 	—1c. now, introductory, 701; 	—1d. so then, in encouraging or summoning; 	—1e. now, pray, in questions, 521, 718, 5120, 748, 7812; 	—2. asseverative: nakir nu, surely no one or nothing, 7320; mā́ nú, in order that surely not, 8610; 	—3. w. relatives: yā nu, whatsoever, 742; yān nu, i. e. yāt nu, as long soever as, 7913. [in V. often nū́: cf. νύ, νῦν, Lat. nun-c, Ger. nu, nun, AS. nu, nū, Eng. now: see also náva, nū́tana, nūnám.]
नुद्: √nud (nudáti, -te; nunóda, nunudé; ánutta [881]; notsyáti, -te; nuttá, nunná; -núdya). push; thrust. + parā, thrust away; move from its place. + pra, push forward; set in motion. + vi, drive asunder or away; turn away, esp. from cares, like the Eng. di-vert; amuse. [for mg, cf. also dis-port and s-port.]
नूतन: nū́tana, a. of now; recent; young. [nú, 1245e.]
नृ: nṛ́ [370, 3715, 9, 10], m. man; hero; used also of gods: of the Maruts, 744, 7718. [cf. ἀνήρ, stem ἀνερ, ‘man’; Old Lat. nero, stem nerōn, ‘manly, strong’; Lat. Nero.]
नृत्: √nṛt (nṛ́tyati, -te; nanárta; ánartīt; nartiṣyáti; nṛttá; nártitum; nartitvā́ ). dance.
नृप: nṛ-pa, m. protector of men, i. e. prince, king.
नृपति: nṛ-páti, m. lord of men, i. e. prince, king. [acct, 1267a.]
नृम्ण: nṛmṇá, n. virtus, manliness, courage, strength. [fr. nṛ (1224c), as virtus fr. vir.]
नेत्र: netra, n. eye. [‘leader,’ √nī, 1185a: for mg, cf. nayana.]
नेद्: néd, adv. lest, in order that not, w. accented verb (595d) in the subjunctive (581e), 8417. [ná + íd, 1111a2.]
नैरुक्त: nairukta, a. pertaining to the Nirukta; as m. an etymologist. [nírukta, 1208f.]
नैषध: naiṣadha, a. pertaining to Nishadha; as m. prince of the Nishadhans, i. e. Nala. [niṣadha, 1208f.]
नो: nó, adv. and not, 2114; no ced, and if not, see ced. [ná + u.]
नौ: naú [361a], f. boat; ship. [cf. ναῦς, Lat. nāvis, ‘ship’; perhaps AS. naca, ‘skiff’: perhaps ‘the swimmer,’ √snū, cf. √snā.]
न्यग्रोध: nyag-ródha, m. Ficus índica, banyan tree. [‘downwards-growing’: nyañc (1249a) + rodha.]
न्याय: nyāyá, m. 	—1. (that to which a thing goes back, i. e.) rule, norm; 	—2. (that in which a thing goes, i. e.) way; 	—3. esp. the right way, propriety. [√i + ni, 1148. 2.]
न्याय्य: nyāyya, a. regular, normal, right; -am, adv. rightly; properly. [nyāyá, 1211.]
न्यास: nyāsa, m. a putting down, commitment. [√2as + ni, ‘throw down.’]
